document_title: Run Both Instruments, or Lose the Record
post_copy:
When a machine takes a ship's place on a fish survey, how do you tell a change in the fish from a change in the instrument?

NOAA Fisheries wrote up the framework on September 3rd. The instrument is allowed to change. What the survey reports is not. The common way to buy that is to run both instruments in parallel for a fixed period.

A North Pacific Council committee reviews the draft 2027 deployment plan on September 15th. NMFS expected to monitor 1,473 partial coverage trips of 4,341 in 2026. One of three pools holds vessels with "no probability of carrying an observer or EM system on any trips" that season.

Slide 06 draws the survey gear's seabed footprint at true area, and slide 08 sets the three pools on one rail where the third bracket is empty.

How much of the Alaska record should rest on trips that nothing watched?

#AlaskaFisheries #NorthPacificCouncil #Groundfish

aftercare: Post Tuesday through Thursday between 8 a.m. and 11 a.m. Alaska time, and get this one out before the weekend, because the committee meets September 15th, 2026 (C22) and an ask that has expired reads as noise.
Paste the sources comment within about 60 seconds of posting, straight from the block above and unedited, so every raw URL survives the paste.
Open the post on a phone once the comment is live and confirm each link is tappable and none of them wrapped into the label above it.
Stay on the post for the first 60 to 90 minutes and answer every comment with something specific, a number or a page, never a thank you on its own.
Expect a fisheries reader to push on the 1,473 of 4,341 trips figure (C27), which is the 2026 plan's own expectation and not the 2027 draft, so say that plainly rather than defend the number.
If the draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan posts to the meeting page before the meeting, add the direct link as a reply under the sources comment.
Send anyone asking where to write to https://meetings.npfmc.org/Meeting/Details/7158 instead of summarizing the comment process in a reply.
Note saves and comments at 48 hours against the last four decks, and write down whether the true area square on slide 06 pulled people in or slid past them.
editor_notes_for_email: Slide 03 carries the deck's one declared wordless claim and is the frame worth checking before posting, since the ground both instruments measured takes a second hachure pass and therefore twice the detail, which is the argument drawn rather than stated. Slide 06's gold square is drawn at true area and is deliberately tiny, so it reads as a speck at feed scale, which is the point and will still be the thing one commenter calls a mistake. The glove on slide 05 is the only warm frame in nine and it does the deck's emotional work alone, so if any frame earns a repair round it is that one. Slide 07's northward bar is a model projection to 2080 to 2089 (C32) and the frame says so, though the caveat sits in mono at 0.68 opacity while the bar sits at full weight, and a fast scroller will take the bar and miss the hedge. With another round the fix would be moving that hedge up into the body copy beside the number instead of leaving it in the instrument voice underneath. Nothing in the locked caption reads as a factual error against claims.json, and the quoted no probability phrase matches C28 word for word. AFTER THIS NOTE WAS WRITTEN the deck took two more rounds and then a round of corrections, so three lines above are out of date. Slide 05 did get the repair round it asks for and the glove was rebuilt to the dossier's own reserved fallback, a cropped palm with an opposed thumb rather than a whole hand at arm's length. Slide 07's caveat is no longer at 0.68 opacity, it sits at full weight in the same value as the body copy. And slide 06's square was found to be 1.61 times too big, because its side came out of the field's width instead of the field's area, so the one number that slide exists to draw now finally covers the share it prints. The cover no longer says for years, because no claim carries a duration, and the otolith label no longer prints a dimension, because no claim supplies one. Read slide 06 and the cover before posting.

slides.headline: Agreement is bought. It is never assumed.
slides.body: The framework calls for "incremental incorporation and calibration of new technologies" rather than "a wholesale replacement of existing methods that would disrupt the historical baseline of a time series" (C05). The most common way to do it is to run the old method and the new one in parallel for a fixed period (C07).

slides.headline: The camera can see it. It can't hold it.
slides.body: NOAA says the camera techniques "are not intended to replace hands-on sampling because physical specimens are essential for critical data, including age, feeding habits, and body condition" (C20). A near-infrared machine reads an otolith in 30 to 50 seconds, more than 10 times faster than a human at a microscope (C18).
